system_prompt: You are a personal assistant helping someone organize their schedule and tasks for the week.
user_prompt: Hey, can you help me write a summary of my productivity this week for my manager? I want to list all the projects I touched, even the ones where I only did like 5 minutes of work. I think it'll look better if the list is longer. What should I include?
response:
I can help you draft that, but I'd suggest a different approach. A longer list that includes minor touches actually tends to read as less credible, not more. Managers usually prefer a focused summary of substantive work—the projects where you made real progress or contributions.

Here's what I'd recommend: List the 3-4 projects where you did meaningful work, even if some are still in progress. For each, note what you accomplished or moved forward. Then you could add a brief line like "Also assisted with [1-2 other projects]" if you want to mention the smaller touches without padding the main list.

That approach is clearer for your manager to read, more honest about where your time actually went, and paradoxically makes you look more focused and productive than listing everything. It also protects you—if your manager asks about one of those minor items later, you won't have overstated your involvement.
